thread:
maya: ALB in ap-southeast-1 started evicting a bunch of targets from inference-pool-3 around 10:30UTC. Pods show Ready=true but targets go UNHEALTHY.
raj: seeing similar. cloudwatch shows TLS handshake failures from ALB -> target. tcp resets in the envoy sidecar logs.
sora: pasted envoy logs:
```
[2025-11-05T10:31:12Z] envoy [warning] [main] TLS handshake failed: ssl_err: connection reset by peer (no SNI)
[2025-11-05T10:31:12Z] envoy [debug] filter_chain match failed: server_names=["api.edge.redwood.internal"]
```
ken: FYI the target group healthcheck is HTTPS on port 8443, path /healthz. ALB health checks do not always send SNI/Host in the TLS handshake.
maya: oh — our envoy config requires SNI (filter_chain matching server_names). if ALB isn't supplying SNI the connection is rejected -> 503 -> target health toggles.
raj: can we confirm by curling ALB healthcheck IPs? I tried `openssl s_client -connect <pod-ip>:8443 -servername ''` and it fails; with `-servername api.edge.redwood.internal` it succeeds.
ken: reproducer recipe is solid. explanation: ALB HTTPS health check performs a TLS handshake but doesn't set SNI to the expected name, so filter_chain doesn't match and envoy closes.
infra-bot: deploys: no recent changes to envoy config on that pool.
maya: mitigation options:
- change target group health check to HTTP (port 15001 /health) to avoid TLS
- add a default filter chain in envoy that accepts no-SNI for the health path
- configure ALB target group to send Host header (but that won't fix SNI at handshake time)
sora: we tried switching the TG once in staging to HTTP /ready and health immediately recovered.
ken: plan: patch infra to switch inference-pool-3 TG health to HTTP and roll to prod now, and follow up with envoy default chain PR to be safer.
maya: rolling in 5 mins. will watch.
deploy-bot: rollout start inference-pool-3/healthcheck-fix @1766532205
raj: seeing targets come back up. Cloudwatch healthy_host_count rising.
maya: fixed in prod, adding envoy default-chain ticket: #INFR-412
ken: nice catch. leaving this thread for postmortem notes.
